Budget.description:
A cap on what one call may spend and how long it may wait.

Every field is optional: a budget with nothing set caps nothing.

max_cost_usd.description:
The most the call may spend, in US dollars, at estimated list prices.

Under a cost cap, a candidate whose price is unknown is never run.
max_cost_usd.title: Max Cost Usd

time_limit_s.description:
The most seconds the call may wait: a cap on waiting, not a latency estimate.

It bounds when web-router stops waiting and starting attempts: a provider call that blocks past it
returns late. The built-in backends clamp each HTTP request to the time left, so theirs do not.
time_limit_s.title: Time Limit S

strict.description: Under a time cap, drop the candidates with no measured p90 latency instead of trying them.
strict.title: Strict

Budget.title: Budget

Candidate.description: One (tool, provider) pair that could serve the call, with what it is estimated to cost and take.

provider.description: The backend that would serve it, by registry name.
provider.title: Provider

est_cost_usd.description: Its estimated cost in US dollars, at list price. ``None`` when unknown or billed by tokens.
est_cost_usd.title: Est Cost Usd

est_latency_s.description: Its p90 latency in seconds, as measured by the provider scans. ``None`` when unmeasured.
est_latency_s.title: Est Latency S

id.description: ``tool:provider``, the name every decision field uses. Filled in when left empty.
id.title: Id

Candidate.title: Candidate

description:
What a router is shown for one call.

Later versions add fields: a router must ignore the ones it does not know.

prompt.description: The query for search, answer and research; the URLs, one per line, for extract; the task for browse.
prompt.title: Prompt

candidates.description: Every (tool, provider) pair that could serve the call and that the budget allows.
candidates.title: Candidates

deadline_s.description: Seconds the router has to answer before the static order is used instead.
deadline_s.title: Deadline S

urls.description: The URLs the call names: extract's URLs, or browse's ``start_url``.
urls.title: Urls

budget.description: The call's budget, when it has one.

pinned_tool.description: The method the caller called. Set, the router orders backends only and does not change the tool.
pinned_tool.title: Pinned Tool
